title: Quantum Tunneling & Flash Memory: Mind-Blowing Physics
tags: What is inside the memory card
How does a flash drive works
How data is stored in computers
description:
Every time you save a photo, song, or document on a USB stick, SD card, or smartphone, you’re relying on a tiny but powerful invention: flash memory. But how does it actually work?

In this episode of Miracles of Science, Pale Blue Thoughts breaks down the fascinating science of flash memory — from its invention in 1980 by Toshiba’s Fujio Masuoka, to the quantum mechanics that makes it possible.

Unlike normal computer chips that “forget” everything when the power is off, flash memory uses special floating-gate transistors that trap electrons even when the device is switched off. This magic trick works thanks to quantum tunneling, where electrons sneak through barriers that should be impenetrable in classical physics. Without quantum tunneling, there would be no smartphones, USB drives, or memory cards.

We’ll explain concepts like:

Binary code (1s and 0s) and how computers store data

Floating-gate transistors and how they trap electrons

Quantum tunneling and why Richard Feynman joked that “nobody understands quantum mechanics”

The limits of flash memory (wear-leveling & durability from 10,000 to 100 million cycles)

If you’ve searched for how flash memory works, USB drive explained, SD card storage science, quantum tunneling memory, or floating gate transistor explained, this video unpacks it all in plain language.
